summary: The Alaska Court System opened nine Fairbanks criminal cases on Sunday, 4FA-26-02109CR to 4FA-26-02117CR, and arraigned eight of the nine the same afternoon. Among them are charges against the two people troopers arrested over a Fairbanks mail theft on Saturday: the counts filed differ from those the troopers announced, with two felony theft counts and no drug count against one defendant and six counts including a Class B felony drug count against the other. Court files were also opened on the four felony arrests Fairbanks police recorded on Saturday, two of them for offences dated Sept. 1. Troopers reported four further Interior arrests on Sunday morning, three of which reached the court record the same day. None of the nine Sunday filings appears in the Alaska Court System's weekly report, whose window closes on Oct. 17; the counts in the filings table below are that report's own, for the week to Oct. 17.

entries.title: Nine Fairbanks criminal cases filed on Sunday, eight of them arraigned the same afternoon
body: The Alaska Court System opened nine Fairbanks criminal case numbers on Oct. 18, running from 4FA-26-02109CR to 4FA-26-02117CR. Eight of the nine record an arraignment held at 1:30 p.m. the same day in Courtroom 102 at the Fairbanks courthouse, before the weekend and holiday judge.

Six felony counts are among them. Roderick Antoino Hill is charged in 4FA-26-02109CR with felony driving under the influence with two or more prior convictions and felony refusal of a chemical test with two or more prior convictions, each a Class C felony, for offences dated Oct. 17 at Fairbanks. Timothy Leland Phillippe is charged on two separate files: 4FA-26-02110CR, theft in the second degree for a value between $750 and $24,999, a Class C felony, and 4FA-26-02111CR, burglary in the second degree, a Class C felony. Both record an offence date of Sept. 1, 2026 at Fairbanks.

Moses Alejandro Luke Gutierrez is charged in 4FA-26-02113CR with assault in the fourth degree for recklessly causing injury, which the file flags as domestic violence related, and with driving under the influence, each a Class A misdemeanour, for offences dated Oct. 18 at Fairbanks. A pre-trial conference is set for Dec. 10 and a trial week for Dec. 21.

The remaining files are set out in the entries below. The weekly report of criminal cases filed, run on the evening of Oct. 17, does not list any of the nine: its window closes on Oct. 17. Every defendant named is charged, not convicted, and every class stated is the one recorded on the court file.

sources.label: Alaska Court System, criminal cases filed

entries.title: Two charged over Fairbanks mail theft after troopers recover insurance cheque, licences and credit cards
body: Alaska State Troopers investigated a report of mail theft involving a Jeep Grand Cherokee in Fairbanks at about 4:37 p.m. on Oct. 17, according to the trooper daily dispatch.

Troopers contacted the occupants, Julia Pitka, 38, and Nolan Peterson, 37, and recovered stolen mail including an $8,000 life-insurance cheque, multiple driving licences and multiple credit cards, the dispatch states. Drug paraphernalia and controlled substances were also found in the vehicle.

The dispatch states that Nolan Peterson was arrested and charged with one misdemeanour count and five felony counts of theft, and one misdemeanour count of misconduct involving controlled substances. Julia Pitka was arrested and charged as an accessory to the thefts, and additionally charged with felony misconduct involving controlled substances and violation of conditions of release.

Court files were opened on both on the afternoon of Oct. 18, and the counts filed differ from those announced. In 4FA-26-02114CR, Nolan Peterson is charged with two counts of theft in the second degree involving an access device or identification document, each a Class C felony, and one count of theft in the third degree of mail, a Class A misdemeanour. No controlled-substance count appears on his file.

In 4FA-26-02117CR, Julia Pitka is charged with six counts: misconduct involving a controlled substance in the third degree for manufacture or delivery, a Class B felony; misconduct involving a controlled substance in the fifth degree for possession, a Class A misdemeanour; two counts of theft in the second degree involving an access device or identification document, each a Class C felony; theft in the third degree of mail, a Class A misdemeanour; and violating a condition of release for a felony, a Class A misdemeanour. No accessory count is recorded on her file.

All counts record an offence location of Fairbanks and an offence date of Oct. 17. Both were arraigned at 1:30 p.m. on Oct. 18 and preliminary hearings are set for Oct. 28 and Nov. 5. Both are charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Fairbanks man charged with felony drink-driving and chemical-test refusal
body: Roderick Antonio Hill, 63, was arrested at the 700 block of Twenty-Seventh Avenue in Fairbanks at 4:22 p.m. on Oct. 17, according to the Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin. The bulletin records two charges, each described by police as a felony: driving under the influence with two or more prior convictions, and refusal of a chemical test with two or more prior convictions.

A court file, 4FA-26-02109CR, was opened on Oct. 18. It records two counts, each a Class C felony: felony driving under the influence with two or more priors, and felony refusal of a chemical test with two or more priors. Both record an offence location of Fairbanks and an offence date of Oct. 17.
An arraignment was held at 1:30 p.m. on Oct. 18 and counsel was appointed from the bench. Preliminary hearings are set for Oct. 28 and Nov. 5. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Man charged on two files with burglary and theft, both offences dated to September
body: Timothy Leland Phillippe, 33, was arrested on a charge recorded by police as burglary in the second degree, a felony, and on a separate row on a charge recorded as theft in the second degree for a value between $750 and $24,999, also a felony, according to the Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin. Both rows are recorded at the 400 block of Cindy Drive in Fairbanks at 12:01 a.m. on Oct. 17, on two case numbers from a series opened earlier in the year.

Two court files were opened on Oct. 18. In 4FA-26-02111CR he is charged with one count of burglary in the second degree, a Class C felony. In 4FA-26-02110CR he is charged with one count of theft in the second degree for a value between $750 and $24,999, a Class C felony.

Both files record an offence location of Fairbanks and an offence date of Sept. 1, 2026 — seven weeks before the arrest rows the police bulletin carries. Arraignments in both were held at 1:30 p.m. on Oct. 18 and counsel was appointed from the bench. Preliminary hearings in both are set for Oct. 28 and Nov. 5. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Woman arrested after troopers say false statements hindered a stolen-firearms investigation
body: Alaska State Troopers state that Helena Cole was contacted during an investigation into reckless firearm use, during which she attempted to implicate another person in the theft of multiple stolen firearms, according to a trooper daily dispatch entry posted on the morning of Oct. 18.

The entry states that multiple stolen weapons were recovered at the scene, that her statements hindered the investigation, and that she was arrested, charged with false information and taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center. The entry gives no date for the incident.

A court file, 4FA-26-02112CR, was opened on Oct. 18 with an arraignment set for Oct. 23 at 8:30 a.m. The file records no charge, no statute, no class and no offence location, so no charge class is stated here. She is arrested and not convicted.

entries.title: Trespass and criminal mischief charged after a burglary-in-progress call on Chatanika Drive
body: Alaska State Troopers responded to a residence on Chatanika Drive in Fairbanks at about 10:20 p.m. on Oct. 17 for a report of a burglary in progress, according to the trooper daily dispatch entry posted on Oct. 18.

The entry states that Christine Guzman trespassed onto the property and attempted to break into the residence by striking a window with a propane tank, and that she was arrested and taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.

A court file, 4FA-26-02115CR, was opened on Oct. 18. It records two counts, both dated Oct. 17 at Fairbanks and both flagged domestic violence related: criminal trespass in the first degree, entering land with intent to commit a crime, a Class A misdemeanour; and criminal mischief in the fifth degree, tampering with property, a Class B misdemeanour. The trooper entry describes the incident as a burglary; the counts filed are trespass and criminal mischief.
An arraignment was held at 1:30 p.m. on Oct. 18. A pre-trial conference is set for Nov. 24 and a trial week for Dec. 7. She is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Five counts charged after assaults at a North Pole business and at the hospital afterwards
body: Alaska State Troopers responded to a business on Badger Road in North Pole at about 11:20 p.m. on Oct. 17 for an assault call, according to the trooper daily dispatch entry posted on Oct. 18.

The entry states that Derek Kelly trespassed at the business before assaulting two employees on the site, that he was transported to Fairbanks Memorial Hospital where he assaulted a hospital security guard, and that he was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.

A court file, 4FA-26-02116CR, was opened on Oct. 18. It records five counts, every one with an offence location of North Pole and an offence date of Oct. 17: criminal trespass in the second degree upon premises, a Class B misdemeanour; three counts of assault in the fourth degree for recklessly causing injury, each a Class A misdemeanour; and violating conditions of release for a misdemeanour, a Class B misdemeanour.
An arraignment was held at 1:30 p.m. on Oct. 18. A pre-trial conference is set for Dec. 10 and a trial week for Dec. 21. He is charged, not convicted. Nobody recorded as a victim is identified.

entries.title: Troopers report a domestic assault and drink-driving arrest at North Pole
body: Alaska State Troopers responded to a residence in North Pole at about 6:37 a.m. on Oct. 18 in reference to a delayed domestic dispute, according to the trooper daily dispatch.

The entry states that it was determined the suspect had committed domestic assault in the fourth degree and driving under the influence, and that the suspect was transported to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.
No person is named in the entry and no court case number is given in it. The person arrested is arrested and not convicted.

entries.title: Arraignment held at a third setting in two-count felony assault case
body: An arraignment in the case against John Edward Raymond Jr, 36, was held at 1:30 p.m. on Oct. 18 in Courtroom 102 at the Fairbanks courthouse, according to the court record. Arraignments listed for Oct. 16 and Oct. 17 were each continued.
A temporary order with release conditions and an attorney order was entered after each of the three settings. The Public Defender Agency was appointed on Oct. 16.

The file records two counts, both Class C felonies dated Oct. 16: assault in the third degree for committing an assault in the fourth degree with two or more prior convictions, which the file flags as domestic violence related, and failure to stop at the direction of an officer with reckless driving. The next event on the file is a preliminary hearing on Oct. 26. He is charged, not convicted.

sources.label: Alaska Court System, Fairbanks daily public calendar

entries.title: Nenana woman arrested on two outstanding warrants and held without bail
body: Troopers at Nenana arrested Natasha Grant, 22, of Nenana on two outstanding warrants at about 10:54 a.m. on Oct. 17, according to the trooper daily dispatch. The dispatch states that both warrants were for failure to remand on an original charge of driving under the influence, and that she was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center and held without bail.

The court record carries both warrants, each issued by the Fairbanks court on Jun. 17, 2026, on two separate files. In 4FA-25-02264CR, which is recorded as reopened, the warrant is recorded as no bail, serve now; the file's first count is driving under the influence, a Class A misdemeanour, on which a conviction was entered after a guilty plea in March 2026, and its docket records a petition to revoke probation and the reopening of the case on Sept. 29.

In 4FA-25-00795CR, a closed file, the warrant is recorded as no bail, remand. That case charged driving under the influence with a blood-alcohol level of .08 per cent or higher, a Class A misdemeanour, on which a conviction was entered after a guilty plea in June 2025; probation was revoked and the case closed in March 2026.
Neither file records the Oct. 17 arrest and no new charge has been filed. She is arrested and not convicted on the warrants, and remains charged and not convicted on what is open in the earlier case.

entries.title: Four Fairbanks cases filed on Saturday, including a drink-driving and test-refusal case at North Pole
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly report of criminal cases filed, run on the evening of Oct. 17, lists four Fairbanks cases filed that day.

In 4FA-26-02105CR, Darius Cyrill Standifer is charged with three counts dated Oct. 16 at Fairbanks: driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance, with a recorded blood-alcohol level of .175, and misconduct involving weapons in the fourth degree for possession while intoxicated, each a Class A misdemeanour; and misconduct involving weapons in the fifth degree, carrying a concealed weapon under the age of 21, a Class B misdemeanour.

In 4FA-26-02107CR, Landon Zachary Bedingfield is charged with driving under the influence and with refusing to submit to a chemical test, each a Class A misdemeanour. Both counts record an offence location of North Pole and an offence date of Oct. 17.

In 4FA-26-02108CR, Gonzalo N Garcia, 23, is charged with one count of driving under the influence, a Class A misdemeanour, with a recorded blood-alcohol level of .157. The police bulletin records the arrest at the 100 block of Fifteenth Avenue at South Cushman Street at 4:43 a.m. on Oct. 17. In 4FA-26-02106CR, Ishi Santana Sarten, 37, is charged with one count of criminal trespass in the second degree upon premises, a Class B misdemeanour; the police bulletin records the arrest at the 2300 block of South Cushman Street at 6:14 a.m. on Oct. 17.
Arraignments in all four cases are set for Oct. 23 at 8:30 a.m. Each defendant is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Second criminal trespass case filed against the same defendant inside a week
body: Two Fairbanks court files six days apart charge Ishi Santana Sarten with the same single offence: criminal trespass in the second degree upon premises, a Class B misdemeanour.

The first, 4FA-26-02072CR, was filed on Oct. 12 for an offence dated Oct. 11; an arraignment was held that day, an appearance bond was posted and counsel entered the case on Oct. 13. Pre-trial conferences are set for Nov. 12 and Nov. 19.
The second, 4FA-26-02106CR, was filed on Oct. 17 for an offence dated Oct. 17, with an arraignment set for Oct. 23. Both record an offence location of Fairbanks. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Troopers forward domestic violence charges to prosecutors after a Fairbanks hotel call
body: Alaska State Troopers responded to a 911 hang-up at a hotel on TVSA Way in Fairbanks on Oct. 16 and found that a domestic disturbance had occurred, according to the trooper daily dispatch.

The entry is typed as assault in the fourth degree, domestic violence, and criminal mischief in the fifth degree. It states that charges are being forwarded to the District Attorney's Office and that the case is ongoing.
No person is named in the entry and no charge is stated in it. A referral to prosecutors is not a charge.

entries.title: Missing Delta Junction teenager has been found
body: A missing-person report filed with the Alaska State Troopers on Oct. 16 for a 14-year-old Delta Junction resident has been closed. The trooper daily dispatch entry now carries the update that the teenager has been found.

The original entry stated that she was discovered missing from her home on the morning of Oct. 16, had last been seen the previous evening, appeared to have left intentionally and might be in Fairbanks.
No offence is recorded. The teenager is a juvenile and is not named here.

entries.title: Troopers forward a theft charge over a mobile phone taken during a Fairbanks disturbance
body: Alaska State Troopers responded on Oct. 13 to a reported non-criminal domestic incident in Fairbanks that had occurred the previous day, according to the trooper daily dispatch entry posted on Oct. 18.

The entry states that investigation revealed a mobile phone had been stolen from one of the reporting parties, that the phone was recovered, that charges have been forwarded to the District Attorney's Office and that the case is ongoing.
No person is named in the entry. A referral to prosecutors is not a charge.

entries.title: Bail review set for Tuesday in three-count methamphetamine case
body: An application for a first bail review was filed on Oct. 16 in the case against William Bruce Ostlund, and a bail hearing is set for Oct. 20 at 11 a.m. in Courtroom 403 at the Fairbanks courthouse.

The file records three counts of misconduct involving a controlled substance in the second degree for the manufacture or delivery of methamphetamine, each a Class A felony, with offence dates of April 21, June 24 and July 8 and an offence location of Fairbanks.
A trial week that had been set for Oct. 19 has been reset. A calendar call is set for Nov. 17 and a trial week for Nov. 30. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Fugitive from justice hearing held and a further hearing set for November
body: A fugitive from justice hearing in the case against Brenden James Clarke was held on Oct. 15 at 1:30 p.m. in Courtroom 102 at the Fairbanks courthouse. The court entered a temporary order with conditions of release, an attorney order and a fugitive from justice temporary order the same day, and counsel entered an appearance on Oct. 16.
A further fugitive from justice hearing is set for Nov. 17 at 1:30 p.m.

The file records one count under AS 12.70.120, arrest prior to requisition, with an offence location of Fort Wainwright and an offence date of Sept. 18. No Alaska criminal charge is recorded against him on the file.

entries.title: Omnibus hearing and trial week reset in evidence-tampering case
body: An omnibus hearing set for Nov. 5 and a trial week set for Nov. 23 in the case against Amanda Elizabeth Moff are both recorded as reset. An omnibus hearing is now set for Dec. 1 at 1:30 p.m. in Courtroom 305 and a trial week for Dec. 14, both before a different judge.

The file records one count of tampering with physical evidence to prevent a proceeding, a Class C felony, with an offence location of Fairbanks and an offence date of Sept. 22. She is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Charges now recorded in two Fairbanks files that had been opened with no charge stated
body: Two Fairbanks cases opened on Oct. 16 with the entry "charging document pending or not filed" now carry charges in the Alaska Court System's weekly report and in the court's online record.

In 4FA-26-02093CR, Susan La Vern Waite is charged with one count of driving under the influence with a blood-alcohol level of .08 per cent or higher, a Class A misdemeanour, with a recorded level of .152, for an offence dated Oct. 15 at Fairbanks. The trooper daily dispatch records a drink-driving arrest under the name on Oct. 15 after a vehicle went into a ditch at Farmers Loop.

In 4FA-26-02094CR, James Ritchie Hollen is charged with one count of driving with a licence cancelled, revoked or suspended after a previous conviction, a Class A misdemeanour, for an offence dated Oct. 15 at Fairbanks.
A third file opened the same day, 4FA-26-02092CR, still records no charge. Each defendant is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Weekly court report lists no cases at Nenana or Healy for the week to Oct. 17
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly report of criminal cases filed, covering Oct. 11 to Oct. 17 and run on the evening of Oct. 17, lists 43 Fairbanks cases and three Delta Junction cases, and has no section for either Nenana or Healy. The run stamp and window were re-checked on the evening of Oct. 18 and are unchanged.

Nenana's most recent filing, 4NE-26-00103CR, was made on Oct. 10 and appeared in the previous week's report. Oct. 10 falls outside the current report's window, and nothing has been filed at the Nenana courthouse since.
Healy has had no section in the report for twenty-two consecutive weeks. Both are low-volume courts for which a week with no filings is ordinary.
